name: Hunter Valley

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

terms: Australia's Geographical Indications nest in three levels: zones, the regions inside them, and subregions inside those.
keyfacts: The Hunter Valley zone boundary largely follows the Hunter Valley catchment, and the Hunter region has three named subregions: Upper Hunter Valley, Broke Fordwich and Pokolbin.
The climate is subtropical with maritime influence, among Australia's warmest wine regions, and more than two thirds of the rain falls from October to April.
Sun and summer storms are the main vineyard challenges, so growers manage canopies to shade bunches without blocking airflow and watch the weather closely before harvest.
Hunter Semillon is unoaked, crisp and delicate with citrus and grass notes when young, and the finest examples turn honeyed, toasty and nutty after as little as five years in bottle.
The Upper Hunter, further inland, is generally warmer than the Lower Hunter and gets less rain.

notes: Hunter Semillon is picked early to make a wine of low alcohol.
Young, it is austere, with lemon, lime, green apple and grassy notes.
With ten years or more in bottle it turns rich and honeyed, with toast, biscuit and a mineral backbone.
Hunter Shiraz is medium bodied, with red and dark berries when young. With age it turns earthy and leathery, and the best can age 20 to 30 years.
Hunter Chardonnay ranges from lean and mineral to full flavored and rich.

blurb.text: One of Australia's first wine regions, in New South Wales, planted from the early 19th century. Known for Semillon, it also makes Shiraz, Chardonnay and Verdelho. The zone covers the whole catchment of the Hunter River.
